description: Run a script on Linux instance to perform for disk investigation.

s3Location.description: S3 location to load the results into bucket

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

ParserID.description: The expression is a comma separated string where each element is a preset, parser or plugin name. To view run 'log2timeline.py --parsers list' or '--info' to list available presets, parsers and plugins.

TargetVolume.description: Target all or specific volumes for forensic analysis. Multiple volumes can be defined as: '1,3,5' (a list of comma separated values). Ranges and lists can also be combined as: 1,3..5. The first volume is 1. All volumes can be specified with: all

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# Disk investigation of a Windows volume. Despite the name this runs on the
# Linux forensic analysis host, against the acquired volume mounted there.
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "DISK_INVESTIGATION_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
# /tmp on Amazon Linux 2023 is a RAM backed tmpfs capped at half of memory, so a
# multi GB plaso storage file written there is RAM taken away from plaso itself.
# createForensicInstance user data mounts a dedicated 512 GiB EBS volume at
# /data, so keep the storage file, the csv and the working directory there.
work_root=/data/forensic-analysis
# $instance was never assigned in this document, so every instance's evidence
# was written to, and uploaded from, the same shared path.
instance=$(printf '%s' '{{s3Location}}' | grep -oE 'i-[0-9a-f]{17}' | head -1)
if [ -z "$instance" ]; then
instance=$(printf '%s' '{{s3Location}}' | grep -oE 'i-[0-9a-f]{8}' | head -1)
fi
[ -n "$instance" ] || fail 'no instance id in the output location - refusing to write evidence to a shared path'
evidence_dir=$work_root/data/{{forensicID}}_evidence_dir/$instance
working_dir=$work_root/data/{{forensicID}}_working_dir/$instance

mkdir -p "$evidence_dir" "$working_dir" 2>/dev/null || { sudo mkdir -p "$evidence_dir" "$working_dir" && sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$work_root"; } || fail "cannot create the work area under $work_root"
# The whole point of working under /data is that it is not RAM. If the EBS
# volume never got mounted, say so instead of quietly filling memory.
fs_type=$(stat -f -c %T "$work_root" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
case "$fs_type" in
tmpfs|ramfs) fail "$work_root is on a RAM backed $fs_type - a plaso storage file there would exhaust memory. Expected the EBS volume mounted at /data." ;;
esac
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 100
cd "$working_dir" || fail "cannot enter $working_dir"
storage_file=$working_dir/log2timeline_{{attachedVolumeId}}_{{ParserID}}.plaso
csv_file=$working_dir/log2timeline_{{attachedVolumeId}}_output.csv
# plaso runs in a container. forensic-analysis-tools.yml installs Docker and
# pre-pulls log2timeline/plaso; it never installs plaso natively, so
# log2timeline.py and psort.py do not exist on this host and this step could
# only ever fail. --user 0:0 because the image runs as a non root user and the
# work area under /data is root owned 0755.
sudo yum install docker -y
sudo systemctl start docker
# The forensic AMI pulls plaso by SHA256 digest and records it at
# /etc/forensic-analysis-plaso-image, then tags it locally as
# log2timeline/plaso:latest so `docker run log2timeline/plaso` resolves to the
# pinned image without a pull. That is deterministic while the pre-pulled image
# is present - but if it is ever absent, the bare reference silently falls back
# to pulling :latest from Docker Hub, which is a different, unreviewed plaso.
# Use the recorded digest and fail loudly instead.
plaso_image=$(cat /etc/forensic-analysis-plaso-image 2>/dev/null)

[ -n "$plaso_image" ] || fail 'no pinned plaso image is recorded at /etc/forensic-analysis-plaso-image - this analysis host was not built from the forensic AMI, and running log2timeline/plaso here would pull an unreviewed :latest from Docker Hub'
sudo docker image inspect "$plaso_image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "the pinned plaso image $plaso_image is recorded but not present on this host"
echo "using pinned plaso image $plaso_image"

sudo docker run --user 0:0 -v /data/:/data -v {{attachedVolumeMountInfo}}/:{{attachedVolumeMountInfo}} "$plaso_image" log2timeline -u --status_view none --storage-file "$storage_file" {{attachedVolumeMountInfo}} || fail 'plaso log2timeline failed'
test -s "$storage_file" || fail 'log2timeline produced no timeline storage file'

sudo docker run --user 0:0 -v /data/:/data -v {{attachedVolumeMountInfo}}/:{{attachedVolumeMountInfo}} "$plaso_image" psort -u --status_view none -o dynamic --dynamic-time --fields datetime,date,time,timezone,macb,type,source,sourcetype,user,hostname,description,filename,inode,md5_hash -w "$csv_file" "$storage_file" || fail 'plaso psort failed'
ls
# Hash only an artefact that exists and carries data: sha256sum of a missing
# file still writes a zero byte _sha256.txt, which was then uploaded as if it
# were evidence for a timeline that had never been produced.
test -s "$csv_file" || fail 'psort produced no csv timeline - not publishing a hash for it'
sha256sum "log2timeline_{{attachedVolumeId}}_output.csv" > "log2timeline_{{attachedVolumeId}}_output_sha256.txt" || fail 'cannot hash the csv timeline'
ls
aws s3 cp "$working_dir" {{s3Location}} --recursive || fail 'uploading the analysis output to S3 failed'
echo s3 cp complete
ls -ltr
exit 0;
